title: The Year Shibusawa Eiichi Left the Finance Ministry to Run a Bank
conflicts: Ono failure date: the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica says the Ono house closed its doors in 1874; Kahm's UCLA dissertation dates the Ono bankruptcy to 1875 (shares off the register August 1875). The story says it closed its doors in 1874 and does not date the formal bankruptcy. Kahm is internally inconsistent on Shibusawa's founding shareholding (500 in text, 400 in table) and on the capital reduction ('by 1.5 million yen' vs shares falling to 15,000), so the story gives neither figure. Reasons for resigning differ by source (could not do what he wanted; political manoeuvring; to promote private business); the story attributes each rather than choosing one.
notes: Capital figures (Mitsui and Ono 1 million yen each, public bought under half of the rest, 2,440,800 yen from 71 shareholders), the 70 per cent government-deposit share, the 'throwaway stone' phrase and the two-year deposit withdrawal rest on Kahm's dissertation (escholarship.org), which loaded for the researcher but returns 403 to the checker; they are attributed in the story to 'a study of the bank's registers'. No founder quotation is used because his autobiography is not available online. Funding 'mixed': merchant-house capital plus a public share offer and heavy reliance on government deposits. Stance 'affirms'.
